title: AWS CDK Rules
summary: Project rules for AWS CDK in TypeScript: construct layers, stable naming, removal policies, assertion tests and a mandatory cdk diff review.
description: This file tells an agent how to organize an AWS CDK app written in TypeScript. It separates reusable constructs from stacks and keeps environment choices out of the construct code.
It also treats infrastructure changes with care: stateful resources are protected, tests assert on the synthesized template, and every deploy starts with a reviewed diff.
useWhen: You start a new CDK app with an agent
A change risks replacing a database or bucket
Stacks hard-code account IDs and regions
You want tests for infrastructure code
body:
# Project rules: AWS CDK (TypeScript)

## Layout
- `bin/` holds the app entry, `lib/constructs/` reusable constructs, `lib/stacks/` deployable stacks, `test/` the tests. Keep stacks thin and put logic in constructs.
- Prefer L2 constructs. Drop to L1 (`Cfn*`) or escape hatches only with a comment saying what the L2 lacks.
- Pass environment as props (account, region, stage) from the app file. Never read `process.env` inside a construct and never hard-code account IDs.

## Naming and state
- Do not set physical names (`bucketName`, `tableName`) unless a cross-stack contract demands it; a fixed name blocks replacement.
- Set `removalPolicy: RETAIN` on databases, buckets and key stores in production, and enable point-in-time recovery or versioning.
- Split stateful and stateless resources into separate stacks so a code change cannot replace data.
- Tag every stack with `owner` and `stage`.

## Security
- Grant access with `grantRead`, `grantWrite` and similar methods. Write a raw IAM statement only when no grant exists, and never use `*` for both actions and resources.
- Keep secrets in Secrets Manager or SSM; reference them, do not inline values.

## Tests and delivery
- Use `Template.fromStack` with `hasResourceProperties` for key assertions, and snapshot tests sparingly.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test`, `npx cdk synth` and `npx cdk diff` before finishing. Report any resource marked for replacement or deletion and wait for approval.

example.prompt: Add a queue and a worker Lambda that reads from it
example.result: The agent adds a QueueWorker construct, grants consume access with grantConsumeMessages, adds a dead-letter queue, writes a Template assertion test and shows the cdk diff with no replacements.

faq.question: Why avoid fixed resource names?
faq.answer: CloudFormation cannot replace a resource whose name is fixed, so an update that needs a new resource fails. Generated names avoid that trap.

faq.question: Can I use it with Python CDK?
faq.answer: The principles carry over, but the layout and test commands here are for TypeScript. Adjust the commands if you use another language.

access: Guidance only; the agent runs cdk synth and diff locally if you allow it, and never deploys by itself
